interpretations: Per-type averages use AVG(unit_price) grouped by production_type_code, ignoring NULL prices. The overall average is AVG(unit_price) over all products with a non-null price. Keep types whose average is strictly above the overall average. The mean of the kept types' averages is the simple mean of those per-type averages, not weighted by product count. Keep only the kept types whose average is strictly above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types:
AVG(type average price).
AVG(type average − overall average).
AVG(type average − mean of kept types' averages).

Same as 1, but "if that average exists" means returning no rows, or NULL values, when the overall average is NULL because there are no non-null prices.
Same as 1, but "ignoring missing prices" also excludes zero or empty-string prices, not just NULLs.

Same as 1, but production_type_code values that appear in Products without a matching row in Product_Categories are handled differently. For example, group over Product_Categories and include categories that have no products.
Same as 1, but the third value is read as the percentage or ratio by which the type average exceeds the overall average, or exceeds the kept-types mean, rather than the absolute difference.
Same as 1, but the second filter's "mean of the kept types' averages" is computed over all types, not only those kept in the first step.
Same as 1, but the three values are returned as separate rows, or only for a single remaining type, rather than as one row of averages.
Same as 1, but if no types remain after the filtering, the result is one row of NULLs. Otherwise it is an empty result.

Same as 1, but the second filter's mean is computed over the types kept in step one, and the types are compared to it with the mean recomputed after the filter (iterated until stable).
Same as 1, but the third value is the difference between the type average and the mean of the kept types' averages taken as an absolute value (the distance in either direction).
Same as 1, but "types" are defined by Product_Categories.product_type_description rather than production_type_code, so codes sharing a description are merged.

queries:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT p.production_type_code AS code, AVG(p.unit_price) AS avg_price, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Products p
  GROUP BY p.production_type_code
  HAVING AVG(p.unit_price) IS NOT NULL
),
k AS (
  SELECT * FROM t
  WHERE avg_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL)
),
r AS (
  SELECT * FROM k
  WHERE avg_price > (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM k)
)
SELECT AVG(r.avg_price), AVG(c.vat_rating), AVG(r.cnt)
FROM r
JOIN Product_Categories c ON c.production_type_code = r.code;
SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM (SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products GROUP BY production_type_code)
SELECT AVG(type_avg - (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM Products)) FROM (SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS type_avg FROM Products GROUP BY production_type_code);
WITH type_avg AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM Products
  GROUP BY production_type_code
)
SELECT AVG(avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM type_avg))
FROM type_avg;
SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM (SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products GROUP BY production_type_code);
